title: Sample Paper: Curriculum Pretraining for Sparse-Reward Reinforcement Learning
abstract: We study whether curriculum-based pretraining improves sample efficiency in sparse-reward navigation tasks. We propose a two-stage curriculum that first trains on dense-reward proxy tasks before transferring to the sparse target task. Experiments on a 2D maze suite show 2.3x improvement over a from-scratch baseline.

sections.heading: Introduction
paragraphs: Sparse-reward exploration remains a long-standing challenge in reinforcement learning. Prior work has explored intrinsic motivation, hindsight experience replay, and curriculum learning as separate remedies.
We hypothesize that a structured curriculum of dense-reward proxies provides the agent with reusable skills that transfer to the sparse target task.

sections.heading: Method
paragraphs: Stage 1 trains the policy on dense-reward shaping. Stage 2 fine-tunes on the sparse-reward target with a KL constraint to the Stage 1 policy.
We use PPO with a shared encoder; the encoder is frozen during Stage 2 to preserve representations.

sections.heading: Experiments
paragraphs: We evaluate on MiniGrid mazes of sizes 6x6, 10x10, and 16x16. Sample efficiency is measured as the number of environment steps to reach 80% success rate.
Our method achieves 80% success in 1.2M steps on 10x10 vs. 2.8M for the from-scratch baseline.

sections.heading: Conclusion
paragraphs: Curriculum pretraining yields substantial sample-efficiency gains; the KL constraint is critical when transferring to harder mazes.

citations.raw: Schulman et al., Proximal Policy Optimization, 2017.
Andrychowicz et al., Hindsight Experience Replay, 2017.
